decision: closed_no_credit: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use.
summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Per the shared OA supplement standard and Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling (ACR 2026 strongly against glucosamine and chondroitin; VA/DoD 2026 insufficient evidence), glucosamine sulfate closes as completed no-credit on the reference path, matching INGR_CHONDROITIN_SULFATE. True directions are kept: the umbrella review 33488785 found high-certainty Lequesne and joint-space benefits with prescription crystalline glucosamine sulphate 1500 mg/day and very-low-certainty pain benefit, and 40005447 pooled SYSADOAs; these exact-preparation findings do not create retail credit. The existing hydrochloride exclusion is unchanged and no new applicability is added. This removes Evidence points from glucosamine products.

record_updates.effect_direction_rationale: Shared OA supplement standard (2026-10-28): the ACR 2026 guideline strongly recommends against glucosamine, chondroitin and their combination for knee, hip and hand OA (certainty low for glucosamine alone, moderate for the combination), and the VA/DoD 2026 guideline (Recommendation 30) finds insufficient evidence for or against them (very low confidence; effects likely below a clinically meaningful difference). Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling, glucosamine and chondroitin records use one standard: completed no-credit on the reference path with true source directions retained; exact-preparation findings are recorded but do not create retail-supplement credit.

identity.chemical_form: Glucosamine sulphate, mostly prescription crystalline glucosamine sulphate 1500 mg/day; not glucosamine hydrochloride

population.description: 11 systematic reviews covering 37 RCTs and 3949 participants, mostly knee OA (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2-3 where reported); a few outcomes in general population, spine or TMJ OA.

study_contexts.study_design: Umbrella review of systematic reviews/meta-analyses of RCTs with re-pooled random-effects estimates and GRADE; 9 of 17 meta-analysed outcomes significant versus placebo.

outcomes.name: Lequesne Index SMD 0.363 (95% CI 0.202-0.524), 3 RCTs, 454 participants, GRADE high, favoring GS
Joint space width at 3 years SMD 0.432 (0.235-0.628), JS narrowing SMD 0.41, OA progression OR 0.382 (0.216-0.677); 2 RCTs, 414 participants, GRADE high
Pain SMD -0.646 (-0.91 to -0.382), 21 RCTs, 1772 participants, GRADE very low; after removing 10 high-risk RCTs SMD -0.298 (-0.546 to -0.05), I2 87%, prediction interval -0.84 to 0.28

limitations: Shared OA supplement standard (2026-10-28): the ACR 2026 guideline strongly recommends against glucosamine, chondroitin and their combination for knee, hip and hand OA (certainty low for glucosamine alone, moderate for the combination), and the VA/DoD 2026 guideline (Recommendation 30) finds insufficient evidence for or against them (very low confidence; effects likely below a clinically meaningful difference). Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling, glucosamine and chondroitin records use one standard: completed no-credit on the reference path with true source directions retained; exact-preparation findings are recorded but do not create retail-supplement credit.
No outcome had a 95% prediction interval excluding the null; pain evidence is very low certainty with high heterogeneity and small-study effects.

Effects come from prescription crystalline glucosamine sulphate at 1500 mg/day; the source distinguishes this proprietary stabilized product from OTC/nutraceutical glucosamine and hydrochloride. Retail sulfate equivalence is not established.
The structural outcomes rest on 2 RCTs (414 participants). The umbrella pools overlapping reviews; listed review identifiers are not independent replications.

outcomes.name: VAS pain versus placebo SMD 0.38 (0.18-0.57) within 3 months and 0.22 (0.03-0.42) after 3 months for pooled SYSADOAs; no difference versus active comparators
